description:
FILED s465ba (Opus, round 23).  Both halves are PRE-EXISTING; what #1032
changed is that they became VISIBLE.

HOW THEY WERE HIDDEN, and it is the s435/s438h pattern again ("a fix that
makes values real exposes what was passing on nothing").  `t/op/filetest.t`
line 285 guards eight rows with

    SKIP: { skip "no -T on filehandles", 8 unless eval { -T STDERR; 1 };

On `1fed80b` that `eval` DIED â `-T STDERR` emitted the bare CL symbol
STDERR, an unbound variable (#1032) â so the block SKIPPED and its rows were
reported `ok`.  With #1032 the gate RUNS and four of the eight fail honestly.
The file's row TOTAL is unchanged (434 either way): 184/250 -> 180/254, four
manufactured passes becoming four honest failures, none appearing or
vanishing.  Verified end to end: the probe's own gate line prints
"DIES (block skips)" on a `1fed80b` worktree and "RUNS (block executes)" here.

TWO CAUSES, probed against perl 5.40.3 (scratch/p22-filetest-T-handle.pl,
both emission paths):

(a) THE `_` CACHE HAS NO STAT-TYPE.  perl remembers whether the last stat was
    a `stat` or an `lstat`, and dies when `_` is then used by the other one:

        -l $f;      # last stat type = lstat
        -T STDERR;  # -T does a stat, so the type is now stat
        eval { -l _ };
      perl:  DIED "The stat preceding -l _ wasn't an lstat"
      PCL:   RAN (no die)

    and the same for `lstat _` after `-T` on a closed handle.  PCL's
    `*pcl-stat-cache-path*` stores the OPERAND only; it needs the KIND
    beside it, and `p--l` / `p-lstat` must refuse the marker when the kind
    disagrees.  Rows: "-T HANDLE sets the stat type", "-T on closed handle
    resets last stat type".

(b) A STAT THROUGH AN IO REF DOES NOT FILL THE CACHE.

        open my $fh, '<', $f;
        stat "/bin/sh";      # a binary file
        stat *$fh{IO};
        print -T _;
      perl:  1
      PCL:   undef            (and the same after `-r *$fh{IO}`)

    `*$fh{IO}` is the IO slot of a glob â `%p-stat-arg` does not recognise
    it, so the stat neither succeeds nor replaces the remembered operand,
    and `-T _` reads the previous one (or nothing).  Rows: "-T _ works after
    stat $ioref", "-T _ works after -r $ioref".

WHERE: `%p-stat-arg` and `%p--path` in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp are the one funnel
both halves go through (`*pcl-stat-cache-path*` lives beside them), so this is
one runtime change, not two.  Do (b) first â it is a missing operand SHAPE,
which is smaller than (a)'s new piece of state.

ACCEPTANCE: the four op/filetest.t rows above, plus the two rows that already
pass in the same block and must keep passing ("-T _ on closed filehandle
resets stat info" and the `fresh_perl_is` PL_statgv pair).  The snapshot row
`baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv op/filetest.t` was spliced to 180/254 in the
#1032 commit with this task as its cause.

=== DONE (s470bs) ===

SHIPPED in commit "`_` remembers WHICH stat filled it and whether it
SUCCEEDED" (runtime only).  Both halves, and half (b)'s CAUSE IS NOT WHERE THE
TASK POINTED â that is the finding.

  (a) THE STAT-TYPE.  `*pcl-stat-cache-type*` (:stat / :lstat) beside the
      operand; `-l _` and `lstat _` after a plain `stat` now DIE in perl's own
      two wordings.  Reading `_` also SETS the type, as perl's ops do (which is
      what makes op/filetest.t's "-T on closed handle resets last stat type"
      reachable).  A THIRD piece was needed and the task did not name it:
      *pcl-stat-cache-ok*, because perl's `_` after a FAILED stat is an INVALID
      BUFFER â every filetest but -T/-B answers EBADF from it, while -T/-B go
      on to OPEN the remembered NAME and answer ENOENT.  Probed:
      `lstat "/nope"; -e _` is errno 9, `-T _` is errno 2; it is the split
      t/op/stat_errors.t asserts for its `_` arguments.

  (b) THE IO REF.  The task said "`%p-stat-arg` does not recognise it".  It
      never gets the chance: `*$fh` on a LEXICAL handle runs
      `p-dynamic-typeglob`, which found no p-typeglob and STRINGIFIED the
      stream into a glob NAME ("GLOB(0xâ¦)"), so `p-glob-slot`'s IO arm looked
      up a handle of that name, found none, and answered undef.  `stat undef`
      then stat'ed the empty path.  Fix: perl's `*$fh` is the ANONYMOUS glob
      the open created and PCL has no such object, so the handle itself is
      handed through and `p-glob-slot` answers its two meaningful slots from it
      (IO = the handle, GLOB = the operand); every other slot is undef, which
      is perl's answer for a slot a glob does not have.

`-r`/`-w`/`-x` NOW STAT BEFORE access(2), because perl's `cando` reads the stat
buffer â that is what fills `_` (the task's own acceptance row "-T _ works
after -r $ioref") and what makes a missing file answer ENOENT rather than
access(2)'s errno.  The access(2) verdict is unchanged.

Guard rows 58-66 of `Pl/t/bareword-fh-slot-01.t`, including the two NEGATIVES
(65/66: `-l _` and `stat _` after an `lstat` must NOT die).  Inverse-verified
against 027ba9c's runtime: all 7 positive rows differ, both negatives agree.

NOT VERIFIED AGAINST t/op/filetest.t's four rows â the companion leg could not
be run (the machine was shut down).  The next session should run
`tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1 op/filetest.t` and compare against the
baseline in scratch/s470bs/base2.tsv (180/254).


=== AMENDED (s470bs-merge, 2026-09-06) ===
The shipped fix had ONE line too many, and the companion leg caught it.
`%p-stat-cache-operand` SET the remembered flavour on every read of `_`.
perl does not: reading `_` performs no stat, so it cannot change what kind of
stat filled the buffer.  `lstat $f; -e _; -l _` is legal, and so is a plain
`stat _` in the middle of the chain.

The ONE exception is `-T`/`-B`: they OPEN the file and stat the descriptor, so
they DO set the flavour to :stat -- but only when there was a valid buffer to
work from, because a -T that can open nothing performs no stat at all.  Probed
as eleven shapes vs perl 5.40.3 (scratch/s470bs/p24.pl); five were wrong
before, all eleven agree after:

    lstat;-e _;-l _        legal      (was: died)
    lstat;stat _;-l _      legal      (was: died)
    lstat;-e $f;-l _       DIES       (unchanged -- a real stat on a path)
    lstat;lstat _          13 elems   (unchanged)
    stat;lstat _           DIES       (unchanged)
    lstat-fail;-T _;-l _   legal      (was: died)
    lstat;-T _;-l _        DIES       (unchanged -- the -T exception)
    lstat;-l -e _          0          (was: died)
    -l -e path             DIES       (unchanged)
    lstat;-e _             1          (unchanged)
    lstat;-s _;-f _;-l _   0          (was: died)

COST OF THE BUG, measured: t/op/filetest.t carried ONE NEW failing row
("stacked -l uses previous stat, not previous retval", line 125) and its
shortfall went 2 -> 8, because the SKIP block died at that row and took five
more with it.  After the fix: 0 NEW ROW, shortfall 120 = the base tree's,
C 369/65.
Guard rows 67-71 of Pl/t/bareword-fh-slot-01.t (133 -> 143), inverse-verified
against the pre-fix runtime, where four of the five differ.
subject: SILENT WRONG, exposed by #1032 (4 op/filetest.t rows that were manufactured passes): the `_` stat cache does not record WHICH stat filled it, so `-l _` / `lstat _` after a plain `stat` never die ("The stat preceding -l _ wasn't an lstat"); and a stat through an IO REF (`stat *$fh{IO}`) does not populate the cache at all, so a following `-T _` is undef where perl says 1.
